# `policy_versions`

**Tier 4** — decisions — policies, overrides, scenarios · owned by `policy-ui` · `public.policy_versions`

**One row is** One saved snapshot of a project's whole policy bundle, with the bundle it replaced and the hash of both. The audit trail of the /policies grid: what the policies WERE at a moment somebody chose to record, which is what makes a simulation result reproducible from the policy side.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `policy_versions_pkey` |

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `data_edit_policies` |
| Minimum project role | `editor` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — **2 with no predicate** |

Tier 4 — the DECISION plane: what a person or an agent CHOSE, as against the dataset they chose it over and the result it produced. `result-binding` (I8) needs all three, which is why WP 6.3 keeps the results and this package takes the decisions. Audited from WP 6.4: the three statement-grain triggers land beside this sidecar, because `dataPlaneAudit.test.ts` scopes its rule to tables IN the contract and a deferred table's writes are unaudited with nothing to notice (D54). **This is the one decision table `result-binding` (I8) already reaches**: a run stores `policy_version_id` and the verifiable export reads the row back, so the policy half of a reproducibility record is bound where the dataset half has to be reconstructed. The row carries THREE author columns beside `created_by`, which is a denormalised copy of a person rather than a second identity (G1) — kept because a version outlives an account and a deleted user should not erase who made a decision.

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 2 policies here grant access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `policy_versions_read_all` — `SELECT` to `anon`, `authenticated`
> - `policy_versions_insert_all` — `INSERT` to `anon`, `authenticated`
>
> Some of these permit **writes**. See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

## Columns

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | Surrogate key. A run binds to this, so it is the id that makes a result reproducible from the policy side. |
| `project_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The project whose policies these are. |
| `label` | — | `text` | — | — | What a person called this version. NULL where it was saved automatically; there is no generated label, because an invented name for somebody's decision is worse than none. |
| `snapshot` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | THE DECISION ITSELF — the full policy bundle as it stood. Whole rather than a diff, so reading one row reconstructs the state without replaying a chain. |
| `created_by` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The user who saved it, by uuid. The three `author_*` columns beside it are the denormalised copy that survives the account. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When it was saved. Server-stamped, never the client's clock. |
| `author_user_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The author's uuid, recorded a second time. It duplicates `created_by` by design — one of the two came first and neither was removed, and a version row is append-only, so they cannot drift after the write. |
| `author_email` | — | `text` | — | — | The author's email AT THE MOMENT OF SAVING. A denormalised copy, not a join key (G1): the account may be renamed or deleted and the decision still has to say who made it. |
| `author_name` | — | `text` | — | — | The author's display name at the moment of saving, for the same reason as `author_email`. |
| `parent_version_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The version this one followed, so the chain can be walked. NULL on the first version of a project — and NULL is also what a version saved before this column existed carries, so an absent parent is `unknown`, not `first`. |
| `previous_snapshot` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | The bundle this version REPLACED, stored beside the new one. It makes a diff readable from one row rather than two, and it is what lets a restore know what it is undoing. |
| `policy_hash` | — | `text` | — | — | The hash of `snapshot`. What a reproducibility record carries so a reader can check that a bundle they hold is the one a run used, without trusting the id. |
| `notes` | — | `text` | — | — | Free text a person wrote about why. The only column here that carries a REASON rather than a state, and nothing reads it today. |
